7740.stem:
Young’s formula for the required amount of medication for a child aged from one to twelve years of age is:

$$D = \dfrac{yA}{y + 12}$$

Where $D$ represents the child’s dosage (in milligrams), $y$ represents the child’s age (in years) and $A$ is the adult dosage (in milligrams).

The graph below shows the required child’s dosage, using Young’s formula, for a particular adult dosage.

\exfigure{3297_q34_1}

figures.cap: graph of child dosage (mg) against age of child (years), dashed curve
solution sketch: relevant part of graph traced for ages 1 to 12

parts.latex: On the graph, trace over the part of the graph that is relevant for the use of Young’s formula.

It is given that the point $(5, 25)$ lies on the given graph.

Determine the adult dosage for this medication.

criteria: Correctly indicates that age is between 1 and 12

solutions.latex:
Substitute the point $(5, 25)$, that is $y = 5$, $D = 25$, into the formula.
$$\begin{aligned} 25 &= \dfrac{5A}{5 + 12} \\ A &= \dfrac{25 \times 17}{5} \\ &= 85 \text{ mg} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Makes some progress towards the solution
